H430.definition: God, divine beings, angels, supreme God.
H430.origin: Plural of H433; gods in the ordinary sense, but specifically used of the supreme God.

H3068.definition: The proper, personal name of the God of Israel, traditionally read aloud as "Adonai" (Lord) out of reverence.

H7225.definition: In the beginning, chief point, firstfruits.
H7225.origin: From H7218; the first, in time, place, order or rank.

H8451.definition: Law, instruction, teaching — what a parent or teacher directs a student to do, not only a legal statute.
H8451.origin: From H3384; a precept or statute, especially the Decalogue or Pentateuch.

H6944.definition: Apartness, holiness, sacredness — set apart from ordinary use for God.
H6944.origin: From H6942; a sacred place or thing; rarely abstract, sanctity.

H3820.definition: The heart — the seat of will, thought, and emotion, not just feeling as in modern English usage.
H3820.origin: A form of H3824; the heart; also used figuratively very widely for the feelings, the will and even the intellect.

H1288.definition: To kneel, to bless — God blessing people, or people blessing (praising) God.
H1288.origin: A primitive root; to kneel; by implication to bless God (as an act of adoration), and (vice-versa) man (as a benefit).

H6666.definition: Rightness, righteousness — right relationship and right conduct, both toward God and other people.
H6666.origin: From H6663; rightness (abstractly), subjectively (rectitude), objectively (justice), morally (virtue) or figuratively (prosperity).

H4941.definition: Judgment, justice, a legal decision — often paired with tsedaqah (righteousness) as a summary of what God requires.
H4941.origin: From H8199; a verdict (favorable or unfavorable) pronounced judicially, especially a sentence or formal decree.

H539.definition: To confirm, support, be faithful, believe, trust — the root behind "amen."
H539.origin: A primitive root; properly, to build up or support; to foster as a parent or nurse; figuratively to render (or be) firm or faithful, to trust or believe, to be permanent or quiet; morally to be true or certain.

H1980.definition: To walk, go, come, live — used figuratively of a whole manner of life, as in "walking with God."
H1980.origin: Akin to H3212; a primitive root; to walk (in a great variety of applications, literally and figuratively).

H3467.definition: To save, deliver, be victorious — the root behind the names Joshua and Yeshua (Jesus).
H3467.origin: A primitive root; properly to be open, wide or free, i.e. (by implication) to be safe; causatively to free or succor.

H2617.definition: Kindness, steadfast love, mercy — the loyalty and grace shown within a covenant relationship, long after it would be reasonable to give up.
H2617.origin: From H2616; kindness, or (by implication) piety.

H7965.definition: Completeness, soundness, welfare, peace — far bigger than the absence of conflict; everything being as it should be.
H7965.origin: From H7999; safe, i.e. (figuratively) well, happy, friendly; also (abstractly) welfare, i.e. health, prosperity, peace.

H7307.definition: Wind, breath, mind, spirit — the same word for the wind you can't see and the Spirit poured out on all flesh.
H7307.origin: From H7306; wind; by resemblance breath, i.e. a sensible (or even violent) exhalation; figuratively, life, anger, unsubstantiality; by extension a region of the sky; by resemblance spirit.

H1984.definition: To shine, boast, celebrate, praise — the root behind "hallelujah," praise loud enough to be seen, not just heard.
H1984.origin: A primitive root; to be clear (orig. of sound, but usually of color); to shine; hence, to make a show, to boast; and thus to be (clamorously) foolish; to rave; causatively to celebrate; also to stultify.

H571.definition: Firmness, faithfulness, truth — something you can build your weight on, not just a fact that happens to be correct.
H571.origin: Contracted from H539; stability; figuratively certainty, truth, trustworthiness.

H2896.definition: Good, pleasant, agreeable, right — the word God himself uses to describe his own finished work in Genesis 1.
H2896.origin: From H2895; good (as an adjective) in the widest sense.

H1245.definition: To seek, search for, strive after — used both of seeking lost objects and of seeking God himself.
H1245.origin: A primitive root; to search out (by any method, specifically in worship or prayer); by implication, to strive after.

G2316.definition: God — a deity, especially the supreme divinity; figuratively, a magistrate.
G2316.origin: Of uncertain affinity; a deity, especially (with G3588) the supreme Divinity.

G2962.definition: Lord, master, one who has legitimate power — used of God, of Jesus, and, in ordinary address, of any social superior.
G2962.origin: From kuros (supremacy); supreme in authority, i.e. (as noun) controller; by implication, Mr. (as a respectful title).

G5547.definition: Anointed one — the Greek translation of "Messiah," used as Jesus's title and eventually as part of his name.
G5547.origin: From G5548; anointed, i.e. the Messiah, an epithet of Jesus.

G4102.definition: Faith, belief, trust, faithfulness — conviction of the truth of something, and reliance on it.
G4102.origin: From G3982; persuasion, i.e. credence; moral conviction (of religious truth, or the truthfulness of God or a religious teacher), especially reliance upon Christ for salvation.

G1342.definition: Righteousness, justice — the state of being as one should be, especially in right standing with God.
G1342.origin: From G1342; equity (of character or act); specially (Christian) justification.

G4991.definition: Salvation, deliverance, rescue — used of rescue from danger as well as spiritual deliverance.
G4991.origin: Feminine of a derivative of G4990 as (properly, abstract) noun; rescue or safety (physically or morally).

G932.definition: Kingdom, royal power, reign — both the realm and the act of ruling as king.
G932.origin: From G935; properly, royalty, i.e. (abstractly) rule, or (concretely) a realm (literally or figuratively).

G1411.definition: Power, might, strength, miraculous power — the root behind the English word "dynamite."
G1411.origin: From G1410; force (literally or figuratively); specially, miraculous power (usually by implication, a miracle itself).

G2222.definition: Life — especially the full, genuine life God gives, as distinct from mere biological existence.

G1391.definition: Glory, splendor, honor, praise — the visible weight and radiance of who someone truly is.
G1391.origin: From the base of G1380; glory (as very apparent), in a wide application (literal or figurative, objective or subjective).

G3341.definition: A change of mind, repentance — literally "after-thought," a genuine turning, not just regret.
G3341.origin: From G3340; subsequent thought, i.e. reconsideration (moral, feeling of guilt over past sin, and turning from it).

G39.definition: Holy, sacred, set apart — used of God, of the Spirit, and of believers set apart for God's purposes.
G39.origin: From hagos (an awful thing); sacred (physically pure, morally blameless or religious, ceremonially consecrated).

G1680.definition: Hope, expectation — confident expectation, not wishful uncertainty.
G1680.origin: From a primary elpo (to anticipate, usually with pleasure); expectation (abstractly or concretely) or confidence.

G26.definition: Selfless, unconditional love — love as a decision and a direction, not just a feeling that comes and goes.
G26.origin: From G25; love, i.e. affection or benevolence; specially (plural) a love-feast.

G3056.definition: Word, speech, reason, message — John reaches for this word, already loaded with meaning in Greek philosophy, to say Jesus is God's self-expression made flesh.
G3056.origin: From G3004; something said (including the thought); by implication, a topic (subject of discourse), also reasoning (the mental faculty) or motive; by extension, a computation; specially, (with the article in John) the Divine Expression (i.e. Christ).

G4151.definition: Wind, breath, spirit — the Greek counterpart to ruach; the same word carries "wind," "breath," and "Spirit" depending on context.
G4151.origin: From G4154; a current of air, i.e. breath (blast) or a breeze; by analogy or figuratively, a spirit, i.e. (human) the rational soul, (by implication) vital principle, mental disposition, etc., or (superhuman) an angel, demon, or (divine) God, Christ's spirit, the Holy Spirit.

G1515.definition: Peace, harmony, rest, security — the Greek word the New Testament reaches for to carry the full weight of the Hebrew shalom.
G1515.origin: Probably from a primary verb eiro (to join); peace (literally or figuratively); by implication, prosperity.

G2842.definition: Fellowship, joint participation, communion, sharing — life held in common, not just friendliness, but a real, shared stake in one another.
G2842.origin: From G2844; partnership, i.e. (literally) participation, or (social) intercourse, or (pecuniary) benefaction.

G5485.definition: Grace, favor, kindness, a gift freely given — undeserved kindness, the word Paul reaches for again and again to describe salvation itself.
G5485.origin: From G5463; graciousness, of manner or act (abstract or concrete; literal, figurative or spiritual; especially the divine influence upon the heart).

G5479.definition: Joy, gladness, delight — close kin to charis (grace) in the Greek; joy as grace's natural fruit, not a separate achievement.
G5479.origin: From G5463; cheerfulness, i.e. calm delight.
